causedByEc23.consequence: CONFIRMED, the most serious finding in this angle. `el` is bound only inside `case 'intent'` (line 2189). The other six branches — `el.label.rendered` (2191), `el.heading.rendered` (2192), `'label' in el ? el.label : el.title` (2193), `el.start.label` (2196), `el.title.label` (2197), `el.row.cells[rowHeaderKey(el.table)]` (2198) — reference an identifier that is not in scope. nameSourceOf is the declared-total function that A-2's composition, A-2's EP-BUILD CI check (`accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)`), §0C.22-ter's one-line invariant (line 2204), §0C.22-quater's row-branch totality argument, §0C.22-sexies's slot/alternatives argument, §0C.22-octies's totality ground, EC-6's ledger row (line 3210) and §0C.28-sexies item R1 ('unfiltered, resolveInteractive is partial, nameSourceOf's totality is false') all stand on. All of them are now grounded in a function body with six unbound identifiers. This is a regression: the pre-EC-23 text (section0c.v5.bak) bound `el` once before the switch.
causedByEc23.fix: Brace the six remaining cases and bind in each, exactly as the intent branch does: `case 'field': { const el = resolveInteractive(env, ref); return { label: el.label.rendered, from: 'field' }; }` — and likewise for section, option, slot, entry, row. (Necessary but not sufficient; pair it with independentPreExisting #A or the narrowing the comment promises still will not occur.)

causedByEc23.consequence: CONFIRMED. `suffix = suffixFor(env.kind, ref, ref.k === 'intent' ? el : null)`. `el` is bound on the preceding line as `resolveInteractive(env, ref)` with `ref` at the full union; the ternary's test narrows `ref`, not `el`, so the third argument's type is `ElementFor<InteractiveRef['k']> | null` — the flat seven-shape union — where suffixFor declares `WidgetIntent | null`. This is precisely the failure mode edit 7 was written to remove from nameSourceOf, reproduced by edit 5 in A-2 itself, one screen above it. A-2's mechanism is an EP-BUILD CI check, so the composition has to be writable; as written the check cannot be compiled.
causedByEc23.fix: Bind inside the branch instead of testing after: `suffix = ref.k === 'intent' ? suffixFor(env.kind, ref, resolveInteractive(env, ref)) : suffixFor(env.kind, ref, null)`, leaving `el = resolveInteractive(env, ref)` in place for the `renderSuffix(suffix, el, env.body)` argument only, where the union is harmless.

The four-line `suffixFor` declaration was inserted BETWEEN `renderSuffix`'s declaration (2168–2169) and the comment block that documents renderSuffix — 'Each pointer resolves — against `el` when base is element, against `body` when it is body — to a Cell, Measure or Phrase, and contributes its MINTED label: Cell.label, Measure.formatted, Phrase.rendered. independentPreExisting.clause: §0C.22-ter, `resolveInteractive`'s declared signature (artefact lines 2162–2163), introduced by EC-21 and untouched by EC-23
independentPreExisting.evidence: `declare function resolveInteractive<K extends InteractiveRef['k']>(env: WidgetEnvelope, ref: Extract<InteractiveRef, { k: K }>): ElementFor<K>`. `Extract<T,U>` expands to `T extends U ? T : never`, a conditional type, and TypeScript does not infer type arguments from conditional-type positions — inference is skipped and K falls back to its constraint `InteractiveRef['k']`. The argument then checks against `Extract<InteractiveRef, {k: InteractiveRef['k']}>` = InteractiveRef (so it compiles), and the return type is `ElementFor<InteractiveRef['k']>`, which — K being naked in ElementFor's conditional — distributes to the union of all seven element shapes. Narrowing `ref` in a switch branch therefore changes nothing about the returned type. Consequence: edit 7's stated purpose ('resolves el inside each branch so ElementFor actually narrows') is unreachable as long as this signature stands, even after the six free `el`s are bound; `el.heading`, `el.start`, `el.title` and `el.row` remain reads the declared type does not carry. The same non-inference applies to `renderSuffix<K>(d, el: ElementFor<K>, body)` (2168–2169), where it is harmless only because A-2 passes the union anyway.
